principles.name: Twelve-factor app methodology
principles.statement: New applications follow the twelve-factor methodology (config in env, stateless processes, port-binding, etc.)
principles.rationale: Twelve-factor patterns are the lowest-cost baseline for portability, scaling, and operability
implications: No configuration baked into images
No local filesystem dependencies for state
Logs to stdout; aggregation is platform responsibility

principles.name: Composable over monolithic
principles.statement: Prefer composing capabilities from independent, replaceable services over building integrated monoliths
principles.rationale: Monoliths constrain pace and concentrate risk; composable architectures enable independent evolution and team autonomy
implications: New applications publish capabilities via stable, versioned interfaces
Shared business logic lives in a service, not duplicated in consuming applications
Replaceability is a first-class design quality assessed at architecture review

principles.name: Independent deployability
principles.statement: A service can be deployed without coordinating with other teams
principles.rationale: Coordination tax kills delivery throughput; coupling at deployment time is the most damaging form
implications: Database migrations are backwards-compatible until the writer is upgraded
API consumers tolerate at least N-1 producer version
Feature flags decouple deploy from release

principles.name: Stateless services, externalised state
principles.statement: Application processes hold no durable state; state lives in managed stores
principles.rationale: Stateful processes block horizontal scaling, immutable deploys, and routine restarts
implications: Sessions held in shared store, not process memory
Failover is a routine event, not an exception
Restarts have no functional impact beyond brief unavailability

principles.name: Observability is built in, not bolted on
principles.statement: Every service exposes health, structured logs, RED metrics, and distributed traces from day one
principles.rationale: Adding observability retrospectively misses the events most worth investigating
implications: Standard observability libraries are mandatory dependencies
Business-outcome metrics are emitted alongside technical metrics
Incidents are debugged from telemetry, not log-fishing

principles.name: Security shifted left
principles.statement: Threat modelling, dependency scanning, and policy checks are part of the development workflow, not a release gate
principles.rationale: Findings discovered at release are expensive to fix and frequently shipped anyway under pressure
implications: CI pipelines fail on vulnerable dependencies above an agreed severity
Threat models exist for every customer-facing service
Secrets are managed by the platform, never committed to source

principles.name: Infrastructure as code, immutable artefacts
principles.statement: All environments are described in version-controlled code; runtime artefacts are immutable
principles.rationale: Hand-managed environments drift, and drift is invisible until something breaks
implications: Production matches non-production via the same IaC
A deploy is the replacement of an artefact, not a mutation
No manual changes in production environments
